findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: core.py:358 keys on st_mode, and not at all when core.fileMode is false; probed: config false + git add of a 0755 file → 100644, disk key bare, _digest_in_index equal
findings.message: `os.access(X_OK)` keys by whether the caller may execute, while git keys by `st_mode & 0111` under `core.fileMode`; on a FAT/exFAT/WSL mount, where git sets fileMode=false itself and every file reports +x, a newly baselined path keys `exec:` on disk and bare in the index/HEAD (probed: same_key → False), so no baselined path retires by commit — the symlink class of retro 0002 for the whole baseline; an owner-only 0o700 file read by another uid mismatches the same way.
findings.minimal_fix: key on `os.stat(full).st_mode & 0o111`, and not at all when `git config --bool core.fileMode` is false

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 3: core.py:357 `st_mode & 0o100`; probed on the archive: 0655 → bare key == _digest_in_index == _digest_at(HEAD), 0711 → exec: on all three, same_key True for both
findings.message: Git records 100755 only when the owner bit is set (`ce_permissions`: `mode & 0100`), but the key tests `& 0o111`; a baselined 0655 or 0611 file keys `exec:` on disk and bare in the index and at HEAD (probed: same_key → False for both), so it never retires by commit — the class round 1 named, on a narrower input, and the comment 'as git reads it' is false.
findings.minimal_fix: test `st_mode & 0o100` (S_IXUSR), and say so in the comment

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: checks.py:1079 `(?!.*\[no tests to run\])`; probed: coverage+norun → no match, mixed two-package output → match; two locks added
findings.message: The lookahead is anchored right after the duration, but with -cover Go prints `ok  \tpkg\t0.004s\tcoverage: 0.0% of statements [no tests to run]` (coverage precedes norun in test.go's Fprintf), so a filter that matched nothing on any Go project testing with -cover/-coverprofile still reads `ran` — the false green R-11 exists to stop.
findings.minimal_fix: use `(?!.*\[no tests to run\])` (`.` stays line-bound under re.M); probed: coverage line → none, mixed output → ran

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: scaffold.py:612 marker is `@.aegis/generated/rules.md` for CLAUDE.md and the bare path for AGENTS.md, matching __main__.py:357-360 and checks.py:1422/1426
findings.message: The comment says 'as migrate tests it', but migrate (__main__.py:357) and check_pointers (checks.py:1422) test `@.aegis/generated/rules.md` for CLAUDE.md; a CLAUDE.md that names the path in prose without the import gets no pointer and the task/merge gate then fails `pointers`.
findings.minimal_fix: use the per-file marker migrate uses: `@.aegis/generated/rules.md` for CLAUDE.md, the bare path for AGENTS.md

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: scaffold.py:392 `underline` is `=`/`-`/`~` only; probed: `Widgets…\n***` returns the prose
findings.message: `***`/`___` now count as rules for the 'title over a rule' drop, but CommonMark makes only `=`/`-` setext underlines; a purpose line directly above `***` is discarded as a title and the next paragraph is drafted instead (probed).
findings.minimal_fix: drop the preceding line only when the rule is `=+`/`-+`; strip the other break lines alone

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 3: core.py:352-359 the stat sits inside the try with file_sha256; probed: os.stat raising OSError → content_key returns None
findings.message: `os.stat(full)` runs outside the `try` that guards `file_sha256`, and unlike `os.access` it raises; a file removed between the hash and the stat tracebacks the gate instead of keying the path as gone.
findings.minimal_fix: move the stat inside the try (one call, `except OSError: return None`)
